newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end up, dollar hits new high vs yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end up, dollar hits new high vs yen.

text.p: The dollar rose to its highest level against the yen in nearly four years on Tuesday, while Tokyo stocks broke a three-day losing streak as investors went shopping for global blue-chip bargains.

Computer-maker Fujitsu Ltd, for one, got a boost from a top brokerage's improved recommendation while consumer electronics giant Sony Corp 6758 T again attracted buyers with high hopes for its satellite broadcasting business plans.

Tokyo's key Nikkei average of 225 leading shares finished up 461.67 points, or 2.66 percent, at 17,796.57, a day high, after falling to 17,195.25 earlier. Nikkei March futures contracts finished 410 points higher at 17,790.

The Tokyo bourse has suffered from uncertainties about Japan's near-term economic growth and lingering woes in the financial industry, and there were worries ahead of the market's opening that the Nikkei could break below 17,000.
But traders said global issues such as Sony and Fujitsu, dubbed the "Nifty Fifty", attracted buyers who finally felt ready to look for bargains.
"High-tech shares are attractive in the current (vulnerable) market. Fujitsu is a core issue in that area," said a broker at a major Japanese securities house.
Brokers said Nomura Research Institute Ltd's upgrading of the firm helped trigger the rise.
Fujitsu gained 30 yen to end at 1,220 yen, its highest since January 5 last year. It was the most actively traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

Sony, which jumped briefly above 8,000 yen for the first time in more than six years, reinforced the Nikkei rebound. Sony was boosted by its announcement last week that it was considering taking part in Japan Sky Broadcasting Co, a satellite broadcasting venture.
"Recent bearish sectors seem to have been sold off enough for now," said Masaaki Higashida, deputy general manager at Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
"The Nikkei 225 is likely to test the upside until it meets with sell orders, aiming to take profits ahead of corporate book closings (at the end of March)," he added.

The dollar, meanwhile, hit a fresh 47-month high of 120.35 yen in late Tokyo trade, encouraged by an apparent lack of Bank of Japan intervention after testing the key 120-yen level earlier in the afternoon.
Most dealers were sceptical about market talk that the BOJ was checking rates in the market, a move that would be a possible prelude to intervention to prop up the yen.
Dealers said further dollar gains were still possible.
"Now the market has lost its sense of 120 yen being a technical and psychological resistance, making people less hesitant about buying," one trust bank dealer said.
The greenback also hit a fresh 31-month high gainst the mark in late Tokyo trade, rising to around 1.6560 marks.
The key March 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract closed lower as new 10-year bonds auctioned earlier in the day were seen as a bit overpriced, traders said.
The March finished at 126.45, down 0.25 from its close on Monday, when it touched a record intra-day high of 126.83.
